Lets break this down as if tones dropped and we got the call.

Arrive at the scene, the man presents as unconscious with sonorous breathing. My first action would be to assess his level of consciousness verbally and the physically, while taking C-Spine precautions (due to the fall)

I would perform a jaw thrust to try to clear the sonorous respiration, while the paramedic checked for a pulse and assess his respiration. If that didn't clear it, and he was still unresponsive, I would use suction and then insert an oropharyngeal airway adjunct and place him on high flow O2, Non-Rebreather if his respirations were above 10/min, or start rescue breathing with a Bag/Valve Mask (ambubag) if they were lower. If there was a gag reflex when inserting the OPA, I would opt for a nasalpharyngeal airway adjunct. Through this process, the medic is putting the monitor on him and assessing perfusion/pallor. We are looking at heart rate, respiration rates, Blood pressure and spO2.

Next, the Medic would check his eyes to determine the condition of his pupils, are they equal and reactive to light. I would continue to assess LoC via Pain stimulus. This would help us determine what his Glasgow Coma score is. With a GCS below 13, we are transporting. We have been on scene now approx 5 mins.

This is where we begin to package him for transport. Maintaining C-spine precautions, we put on a c-collar, perform a quick DCAP-BTLS trauma exam, taking special note for head contusions, depressions, battle-signs/raccoon eyes. Through this, the medic would begin to gather a history from whoever was present and from what we can observe trying to get info on what happened, any allergies, medical history, current medications. name, age, last meal, etc.then and strap and tape him on a longboard and then roll.

I would drive, the medic would be in the back with the patient, inserting an IV, getting fluids on board if, needed. We would be shooting for at minimum, a lvl II trauma center, which for the area I work is approx 35-40 minutes away, driving emergent. The medic would be reassessing every 5 mins en route.
